name: Glitch Art (label normalized from source descriptions; category Digital and 3D Aesthetics). The source does not state a provenance beyond this normalization.
visualIdentity: Built on a clear fault model such as signal interruption, data loss, or displacement. Brief strip offsets, RGB channel separation, and block damage appear at narrative or transition points, then clarity is restored. Continuous random corruption of every element is explicitly avoided.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to short, transition-led edits with a clear fault model. Source suggestions pair it with kinetic typography for tech promos, cybersecurity messages, and punchy social cuts, or with a HUD for sci-fi and security incident explainers. Wider fit is inferred from its brief-event design.
limitations: Glitches must remain brief events, and body copy must not be glitched. Clean text should stay visible for most of the runtime. Glitch only the systems named in the story. Calm editorial scenes, or any case where distortion undermines communication, are poor fits. Simulated appearance is not evidence of physical production.
palette: Reference-dependent example, not an intrinsic style palette: background #111A24, foreground #F2F0E6, accent_1 #47B3AF, accent_2 #D16A84. Gradients are disabled, and tokens apply only to new presentation elements. Task-provided exact colors and source artwork override these values. Two-color opaque checks: foreground on background 15.356, background on accent_1 6.963, background on accent_2 5.101. Recheck composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Video: timed displacement, channel-separation, and localized damage passes act on the rendered image, and the clean source is restored at the end of each event. Suggested events last six to ten frames at transitions. Interactive HTML: one glitch triggered on hover or focus, disabled under reduced motion. Optional motion-020 uses bounded slice offsets, reversible scrubbing, and a reduced-motion cut.
audio: Unspecified by this style, and no music, voice, or sound layer is mandated. Inferred options include restrained sound effects or silence to mark glitch events and reading holds, with music or narration chosen by topic. Honor any user audio request, keep speech intelligible, and avoid clipping. Gallery previews of motion-020 remain silent.
assetRequirements: Requires a rendered source image to feed the displacement and channel passes. Local fonts and assets must load before rendering, randomness must be seeded, and stateful simulations must be cached. No specific asset files are supplied, so missing assets are unspecified. Optional motion references need inspection of actual scene illustrations before selection.
combinations: Glitch Art alone suits short transition-led edits. Supporting style-093 (kinetic typography) provides the clean baseline that glitch events interrupt and restore. Supporting style-112 (HUD) makes a system fault the narrative event, affecting only named panels. Motion-020 is a listed good fit, while motion-012 and motion-015 are optional. Avoid calm editorial combinations.
productionApproach: Style renderer: WebGL with GLSL shaders for displacement, channel separation, and damage, or Canvas 2D image tiles as an alternative. Motion engine: GLSL for distortion, with GSAP only for paused, seekable non-distortion properties in motion-020 transitions. Pipeline: HyperFrames by default; Remotion only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, with the reason recorded. Derive all state from composition time, and verify opening, action, transition, and closing frames plus audio sync and loop continuity.
